text:
Duplex escapement, for watches, so called from partaking of the characters of the spur and crown wheels. The axis of balance carries pallet, B, which at every oscillation receives an impulse from the crown teeth. In the axis, A, of balance-wheel is cut a notch into which the teeth round the edge of the wheel successively fall after each one of the crown teeth passes the impulse pallet, B.

— Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements (1908), no. 293
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 293; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_293.html.

text:
Lever escapement. The anchor or piece, B, which carries the pallets, is attached to lever, E, C, at one end of which is a notch, E. On a disk secured on the arbor of balance is fixed a small pin which enters the notch at the middle of each vibration, causing the pallet to enter in and retire from between the teeth of escape-wheel. The wheel gives an impulse to each of the pallets alternately as it leaves a tooth, and the lever gives impulse to the balance-wheel in opposite directions alternately.

— Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements (1908), no. 296
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 296; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_296.html.

text:
A dead-beat pendulum escapement. The inner face of the pallet, E, and outer face of D, are concentric with the axis on which the pallets vibrate, and hence there is no recoil.

— Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements (1908), no. 303
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 303; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_303.html.

text:
A single-pin pendulum escapement. The escape-wheel is a very small disk with single eccentric pin; it makes half a revolution for every beat of the pendulum, giving the impulse on the upright faces of the pallets, the horizontal faces of which are dead ones. This can also be adapted to watches.

— Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements (1908), no. 305
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 305; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_305.html.

text:
A detached pendulum escapement, leaving the pendulum, P, free or detached from the escape-wheel, except at the time of receiving the impulse and unlocking the wheel. There is but one pallet, I, which receives impulse only during the vibrations of the pendulum to the left. The lever, Q, locks the escape-wheel until just before the time for giving the impulse, when it is unlocked by the click, C, attached to the pendulum. As the pendulum returns to the right, the click, which oscillates on a pivot, will be pushed aside by the lever.

— Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements (1908), no. 308
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 308; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_308.html.

text:
Three-legged gravity escapement. The lifting of the pallets, A and B, is done by the three pins near the center of the escape-wheel, the pallets vibrating from two centers near the point of suspension of the pendulum. The escape-wheel is locked by means of stops, D and E, on the pallets.

— Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements (1908), no. 310
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 310; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_310.html.

text:
Bloxam’s gravity escapement. The pallets are lifted alternately by the small wheel, and the stopping is done by the action of the stops, A and B, on the larger wheel. E and F are the fork-pins which embrace the pendulum.

— Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements (1908), no. 312
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 312; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_312.html.
